title: Secrets and Keys with Azure Key Vault

questions.prompt: A requirement states that an administrator holding Contributor on a key vault must not be able to grant themselves access to its secrets. Which permission model satisfies this?
options: The vault access policy model, with the administrator omitted from all policies
The Azure RBAC permission model
The vault access policy model, with a resource lock applied to the vault
Either model, provided the vault firewall denies the administrator's address
questions.explanation: Under the access policy model, anyone holding Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/write can add a policy granting themselves data-plane access, so omitting them from today's policies changes nothing. Azure RBAC makes data-plane permissions role assignments, creatable only by Owner or User Access Administrator. A firewall does not help: the control plane is not filtered by it.

questions.sub_skill: Configure firewall settings on Key Vault
questions.prompt: You set a vault's network rules to deny by default with no allowed addresses. From your laptop, which operations still succeed?
options: Reading the vault's tags and changing its SKU
Retrieving a secret value
Listing the names of secrets in the vault
Adding a new access policy to the vault
questions.explanation: The vault firewall filters the data plane at <vault>.vault.azure.net only. Control-plane operations go to Azure Resource Manager and are governed by Azure RBAC, so reading properties, changing the SKU, and adding access policies all still work. Reading or listing secrets is data plane and is blocked.

questions.prompt: A lab vault is deleted and the same lab must run again next week with the same vault name. Which configuration choice made at creation determines whether that is possible?
options: The SKU, because Premium vaults are purged automatically
Purge protection, because it cannot be disabled once enabled
The soft-delete setting, because soft delete can be turned off at creation
The permission model, because RBAC vaults release their names immediately
questions.explanation: Soft delete is always on and cannot be disabled, and it reserves the name for the retention period. With purge protection off you can purge the deleted vault and reclaim the name; with it on, nobody can, at any privilege level, until retention expires.

questions.prompt: Which question does Defender for Key Vault answer, and which does Defender CSPM secret scanning answer?
options: Defender for Key Vault finds credentials stored outside the vault; secret scanning detects anomalous vault access
Defender for Key Vault detects anomalous access to the vault; secret scanning finds credentials stored outside it
Both detect anomalous access, at different scopes
Both find exposed credentials, one at rest and one in transit
questions.explanation: They face opposite directions. Defender for Key Vault is a workload protection plan watching the vault's data plane for unusual principals, locations and volume. Secret scanning is agentless discovery of credentials that never made it into a vault, which is usually how lateral movement was possible.

questions.prompt: An application must read one specific secret and nothing else in the vault. Which assignment is least privilege?
options: Key Vault Reader at vault scope
Key Vault Secrets User at vault scope
Key Vault Secrets User scoped to the individual secret
Key Vault Secrets Officer scoped to the individual secret
questions.explanation: RBAC assignments can be scoped to an individual secret, key or certificate, and that is the least-privilege answer people forget exists. Key Vault Reader sees that a secret exists but not its value; Secrets User at vault scope reads every secret; Secrets Officer can also delete.
